thread:
Mike F: quick check — thinking about the proxy eviction routing behavior for overloaded tenants. proposal: prefer local smart-edge pools, evict to hosted fallback only when both latency and quota pressure exceed thresholds. thoughts?

Julia H: prefer local smart-edge for latency makes sense, but worried about bursty tenants hogging reserved capacity. how we define "both" matters. :thinking:

Ara: +1 on needing clear signal math. maybe two signals: (1) latency SLO breach for the route, (2) sustained token consumption > X% of tenant commit for Y seconds. only then failover.

Sarah L: can we tie this into the console rollout UX? operators need to see why traffic moved. audit event + route breadcrumb in dashboard. otherwise support gets flooded.

Mike F: agreed. want a human-readable breadcrumb like: "route_evicted -> fallback=hosted-lowcost -> reason=(latency=120ms>90,quota=87%>80 for 90s)". console should show last 10 evictions.

Nate: on telemetry side, we need a compact event schema we can index. suggestion: {event_type, tenant_id, route, reason_codes[], timestamp, before_pool, after_pool}. keep it small to avoid ingestion costs.

Julia H: +1 on schema. also include a sample rate for high-frequency tenants. we should not emit every single evict/restore event, but bucket them. Eg: emit full event on first, then aggregate counts per minute.

Ara: operational question: when we fall back to hosted, do we also downgrade model variant (quantized) automatically? that might reduce cost but change outputs. should be opt-in per tenant.

Sarah L: must be opt-in. any automatic model change needs eval gating and customer consent. At least show in console that fallback will use variant X if enabled.

Mike F: new config idea (in YAML):
```
eviction_policy:
  prefer_local: true
  latency_threshold_ms: 90
  quota_threshold_pct: 80
  sustained_secs: 90
  fallback_steps:
    - type: pool_swap
      target: hosted-lowcost
    - type: model_variant
      target: gpt2q-8bit
      enabled: false
  telemetry:
    sample_rate: 0.1
    aggregate_window_s: 60
```

Nate: looks good. one note: sample_rate 0.1 might undercount for small tenants. recommend per-tenant override and system default 0.25 for tenants > TPS threshold.

Julia H: also need a canary rollout for changing policy global defaults. we can't flip eviction math without impact analysis. expose a rollout flag in console with A/B groups.

Sarah L: UX: show expected cost delta on the policy panel (estimate tokens * cost-per-token for fallback vs local). even a rough estimate helps CS.

Mike F: agreed. For the gateway shape, is everyone okay with a thin proxy that only handles routing decisions + telemetry, and the heavy logic (quota evaluation, sustained detection) in a central decision service?

Ara: yes for thin proxy. keep proxies infra-light and cache decisions from central service. but cache TTL needs jitter and invalidation hooks for quick restores.

Nate: caching decisions needs idempotent keys: tenant_id + route + decision_version. add a changefeed from control-plane to proxies so we can invalidate by version.

Julia H: rollbacks: add a safemode where proxies auto-revert to previous decision on error rates > 3% for 2 minutes. simple circuit-breaker.

Mike F: nice. final checklist before I draft an RFC:
- telemetry schema and sampling plan (Nate)
- eviction config shape and per-tenant overrides (me + Julia)
- console breadcrumbs + cost estimate UX (Sarah)
- model-variant opt-in workflow (product)
- rollout/canary plan + safemode (Julia + Ara)

Sarah L: I'll mock a console panel tomorrow and include screenshot placeholders.

Mike F: thanks all — will drop RFC link once I have the draft. :thumbsup:
